summary: This article presents a differential benchmark of three open-source GitHub issue-form body parsers across 19 synthetic test cases containing agent-style Markdown constructs. It systematically uncovers significant delimiter collision vulnerabilities, truncation issues, and ordering regressions across all existing implementations. The methodology is rigorous and well-controlled, providing actionable guidance for automations relying on parsed issue form bodies.
strengths: Well-structured differential testing methodology with clearly isolated variables, negative controls, and defined oracles.
Uncovers actionable failure modes, such as the unterminated fence regression in stefanbuck v3.2.5 and ordering-dependent injection vulnerabilities.
Provides a thorough explanation of the root cause: unescaped markdown delimiter collisions inherent to GitHub's issue form serialization.
Clear presentation of results with an informative summary matrix and precise failure classification (FIELD_CHANGED, DESC_ALTERED, EXTRA_KEYS).
weaknesses: Evaluation relies solely on 19 synthetic test cases rather than mining a corpus of real-world GitHub issues.
The strict reference parser was authored by the benchmark creator and evaluated against the same synthetic test suite, introducing potential design bias.
Only a single four-field schema configuration and one alternative field ordering were tested.
suggestions: Validate the proposed duplicate-label rejection heuristic against a sample of historical, real-world GitHub issue bodies to measure actual false-positive rejection rates.
Expand testing to include more diverse field types, such as multi-select dropdowns and nested Markdown elements.

claims.text: The stefanbuck/github-issue-parser commit cf55537, 'fix: improve body parsing logic (#72)', released as v3.2.5 in April 2026, replaced a split on '###' because it broke on mid-line hashes and on fenced blocks.
When a user submits the form, GitHub writes a single Markdown body. Each field appears as a level-3 heading with the field label, then a blank line, then the value.
@zentered/issue-forms-body-parser is an open-source parser designed to parse question/answer formatted markdown bodies from GitHub issue forms.

novelty_vs_existing.title: LatentMD: LLM Markdown fence-boundary failures
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: While existing literature examines fence-boundary generation errors in LLM output text, this benchmark focuses on the downstream software engineering problem of delimiter collisions and parsing failures in GitHub Actions issue automation pipelines.
